newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank of Italy seen checking mark/lira rates.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy seen checking mark/lira rates.

text.p: The Bank of Italy has been checking mark/lira rates in the foreign exchange markets from about 0830 GMT onwards this morning, at 993.50 per mark and 994.50 per mark area, currency traders said.
The lira was quoted at 994.55/4.85 per mark by 0940 GMT compared 992.60 shortly after European trade started and a morning low of 995.25.
One trader in London said fund selling in early trade drove the Italian currency lower and the central bank had started asking prices all round the market at 993.50.
The lira remained under pressure, hit by nervousness over French elections and rumours that credit agencies were considering Italy's credit ratings.

However traders were cautious about that, noting the market was generally nervous on EMU concerns and rumours were easy to generate. Moody's and IBCA declined to comment on Italy's ratings and Standard & Poor's said Italy was not on creditwatch.

Dealers said the Bank of Italy had later checked rates at 994.50 per mark, and some traders said they thought the central bank had probably intervened to support the lira but they had not actually dealt with it themselves.
